exclusion_detail: Lead 9h (3-(2-chloroethyl) quinazolinone) would be 4 steps (Ac2O benzoxazinone, amine opening, SNAr with 3-(diethylamino)propylamine, Knoevenagel with 4-isopropylbenzaldehyde), but the paper never describes the 3-(2-chloroethyl) intermediate: the only 3-haloethyl intermediates printed are 2b5 and 3b7, both named 2-fluoroethyl (their NMR has two triplets, which would fit chloroethyl, but the printed names say fluoroethyl), and the amine used for 2b2-2b5 is only called 'aliphatic amines'. The 2-chloroethylamine reagent would have to be inferred, so no transcription.

lead.label: 9h
lead.why: Abstract: 'Among them, compound 9h exhibited nanomolar inhibitory activity and binding affinity for BLM'; 9h = (E)-3-(2-chloroethyl)-7-((3-(diethylamino)propyl)amino)-6-fluoro-2-(4-isopropylstyryl)quinazolin-4(3H)-one

notes: Source is main text only (no SI file in bundle); experimental section is in the article. Candidates 4h/6h/7h/8h (3-methyl/ethyl/ethyl+ethylamino/isobutyl) are 4-step routes from 2-amino-4,5-difluorobenzoic acid via Ac2O -> 1b1, amine -> 2b2/2b3/2b4, diethylaminopropylamine (or ethylamine) SNAr -> 3b-series, aldehyde Knoevenagel; the amine for the 3-substituent is implied by the intermediate names rather than stated, so listed with that caveat. Also: 3b7 NMR has a typo ('4.81-1.62').
